extracted.intended_audience: secondary-school teachers delivering BC First Peoples 12 / teacher-educators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and activities for delivering Units 2–3 of the BC First Peoples 12 course, including lesson ideas, assessment suggestions, sensitivity protocols, and specific investigations on storytelling and Indian Residential Schools. Intended to help teachers plan lessons, discussions, and projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Indigenous women's careers (video as starting point)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students research the careers of six successful Indigenous women, using the National Film Board video Doctor, Lawyer, Indian Chief (1986) as a starting point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View the NFB film and the filmmaker interview; use the video as a starting point to find out about the ongoing lives of the women in subsequent decades; select one woman to follow up on how her life evolved after 1986; follow the filmmaker's career as an option. Note: some subjects may be harder to follow up (e.g., Sophie/Lucille MacLeod).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare historical and present-day contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss differences students noticed between 1986 and the present day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompts include: roles of women (would these careers be as notable today?), terminology changes (use of 'Indian'), and fashion. Use these comparisons to frame discussion about social change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze similarities and differences in life paths
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask students to think about the similarities and differences in the life paths of people featured in source material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, note shared experiences (several went to Residential School) and common values (valued their cultures). Use this to prompt deeper biographical or historical inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biography creation — acceptable presentation formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Students can create a biography of an Indigenous person they know or have researched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested presentation formats: write a biographical sketch; create a visual essay; body representation (trace body outline and collage/draw to express aspects of the person's story — adapt Body Biography activity); create a podcast or an 'imaginary interview.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflective learning — Give Back, Carry Forward
rubrics_metrics.description: Students reflect on important learnings in the unit and consider how they can give back and carry learning forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Major Project outline; connect reflections to actionable steps in the community or school.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection prompts — 'What Did You Learn?'
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured reflection prompts to elicit meaningful student responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: What is one new thing you learned that you would consider a gift? What is one thing, growing out of your learning, that you can take action on? What new things did you learn about where you live? What did you learn about yourself?

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting learning and showcasing work
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss and plan ways students can document and showcase their learning while connecting to 'giving back' and 'carry forward' themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage students to develop portfolios, presentations, community projects, or other showcases that demonstrate connections between learning and community action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach truthfully about Residential Schools and impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to talk about the Truth of what happened in the schools and the continuing impacts on Survivors and families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include discussion of healing and responsibilities to take actionable steps toward Reconciliation; emphasize resilience and strengths of Indigenous peoples; make clear the intent is not to blame or shame Non-Indigenous people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher role as guide, not expert
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers are not expected to be experts on the history and legacies of Indian Residential Schools or Truth and Reconciliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers should act as guides and facilitators and bring in knowledgeable community members or resources when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of and respond to student emotional reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that content about Residential Schools can trigger strong emotions and personal reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time to deal with concerns and questions, be ready to refer to counsellors or trained supports, and convey that understanding the past aims toward a more positive future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer discussion-based approaches for sensitive topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitive and controversial topics may be best taught through discussion rather than lecture/instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate discussions that promote understanding and avoid becoming mere exchanges of intolerance; set up supports and structure for safe conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set ground rules for safe classroom discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish expectations to ensure a safe environment when discussing sensitive topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Always respect and value what others bring to the discussion; it is okay to feel discomfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supports and referrals for students
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare to help students deal with difficult emotions by connecting them to knowledgeable supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify school counsellors and Indigenous community resources; notify other educators that the topic will be discussed; when needed, refer to crisis lines (Indian Residential Schools Crisis Line, Kids Help Phone) and list contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning focus — First Peoples Principles of Learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Use First Peoples Principles of Learning as focal learning goals (e.g., learning involves recognizing consequences of one’s actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame activities (e.g., reflection on 'Every Child Matters') to promote consideration of responsibility and accountability personally and collectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content learning standards — required topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify core content learning standards to focus on in the unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested focuses: role of oral tradition for B.C. First Peoples; provincial and federal government policies/practices affecting First Peoples; resistance to colonialism; contemporary challenges and legacies of colonialism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess baseline understanding via quiz/discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess students' base understanding of Indian Residential Schools before proceeding with deeper investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Line Master 3-1 quiz individually then discuss as groups or whole class; alternatively have groups create and test each other with their own questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss historical terminology and its context
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss use of the term 'Indian' when referring to the schools and why it appears in historical sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain as historical terminology (initially targeted at 'status Indians' under the Indian Act), note later inclusion of Inuit and some Métis, and contrast with other kinds of residential/boarding schools sent to by choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localize learning — identify regional Residential Schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be able to identify Indian Residential Schools that operated in their region and where local Indigenous students were sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use regional maps and references (e.g., a map in Grade 10 resources) to contextualize learning locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary activity — Indian Residential Word Sorter
rubrics_metrics.description: Use word-sorting activities to build vocabulary and conceptual connections related to Residential Schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities: cut and sort words into groups, create a word web connecting terms, or write sentences using two words together (Line Master 3-2).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3-Way Summary strategy for concision and synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice summarizing the impacts of Residential Schools at three lengths to develop concision and synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write three summaries: 75–100 words, 30–50 words, and 10–15 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study primary historical documents (e.g., Bryce Report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use primary source documents to understand historical awareness and proposed remedies regarding Residential Schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have students read Bryce reports and related primary sources to identify what commentators suggested to reduce death rates and to analyze government/church responses; links to reports and teaching resources provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and analyze the TRC Calls to Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should review and understand the Truth and Reconciliation Commission’s 94 Calls to Action, including their origins, purpose, and intended audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss who created the Calls to Action, how they came about, their purpose (to guide Reconciliation), and who they target (all Canadians, especially governments and churches); use TRC website and youth versions for study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarize with National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure students know about the NCTR and the types of records it houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have students explore the NCTR website to see holdings and ongoing work; emphasize use of archival records in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify sources and accuracy (critical media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: When using secondary sources such as Wikipedia or news reports, students should verify that information is current and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: check the Wikipedia page 'Canadian Indian residential school grave sites' for currency and corroborate with primary/community sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze memorials and community responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use images and reports of memorials and public gatherings to prompt student reflection and discussion about community responses to findings (e.g., Kamloops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring local images where possible; ask students to reflect on their memories or recall of public reactions and memorials; use linked news articles as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine Indigenous communications for oral traditions and protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze official Indigenous community communications (e.g., Tk’emlúps te Secwépemc news release) for elements reflecting oral traditions, responsibilities, and adherence to protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: What aspects reflect Oral Traditions? Why does the community feel responsibility toward missing children and home communities? How were Protocols followed in releasing the news?

rubrics_metrics.name: Use protocols and traditional knowledge with modern technology
rubrics_metrics.description: When investigating unmarked burials, combine Indigenous protocols/traditional knowledge with appropriate scientific technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read Line Master 3-3 'Protocols and Technology' and a backgrounder on remote sensing and grave detection (written for First Nations) to understand how traditional perspectives and ground-penetrating radar/etc. are used together.
